Title: Ken at the track

Ken is at the track. He has a drink, a back pack and a stack hat.
Ken puts his cap in his back pack. He clips on his red stack hat.
Ken sits at the crest of the hill. “This will be fun!” he thinks.
Ken kicks off. He is quick!
Ken can do some cool tricks. He has skills!
Ken has a cramp in his leg. He skids on the rocks. Crash!
Ken has no bumps or cuts on his skin. He sits for a rest.
Ken has a swig of his drink. “I will get back on the track,” he thinks.

Title: Greyson’s Neighborhood

Greyson lives in a beige house on the corner of Eighth Street and Great Lake Road. He has lived there for eighteen years. Greyson loves his neighborhood because he has great neighbors. Any time he passes someone on his street they always wave and say hey. Greyson’s next-door neighbor is Stewart. Stewart loves to cook and has a huge grill in his backyard. Every Friday, Stewart hosts a dinner party for Greyson and some other neighbors. Last Friday, Stewart grilled steak and corn. It was quite tasty! Greyson’s neighbors across the street are Cosmo and Wanda. They have three dogs, four cats, and one fish. That’s eight pets! Sometimes, Greyson walks the dogs for Cosmo and Wanda if they need a break. When Greyson walks the dogs, they always go straight to the park to play fetch. Greyson loves his beige house, his nice neighborhood, and his friendly neighbors. He thinks he just might stay there for another eighteen years.

Title: The Stampede

It was an extremely hot evening. Jolene is an athlete, and her game
ended late. She was driving home hot and tired. She just wanted to go to
bed. All of a sudden, she had to stop. There were buffalo everywhere!
A stampede thundered on the pavement around her small car. The herd
was in a frantic run. Her little vehicle rattled and jiggled along with the
concrete under her. She felt like the size of a centipede compared to the
size of these massive buffalo!
The animals rushed by. Something must have startled them and made
them run. She could only see a sphere-shaped object to her left, but she
could not see what it was. It was so dark!
Jolene was a little scared. The buffalo merely had to brush the side and
the car would rock. They could crush her car! She had a string of things
going through her mind: “Am I safe here in my car? Should I try to drive?
I can’t think of who I can call to help! I don’t understand what is going on!”
Moments later, the dust began to settle. The last of the buffalo passed by
her. She had never felt like this in all of her life. How and why did that
happen? She would have this scene stuck in her mind forever. Jolene
would never forget the stampede.

Title: A Visit to the Pacific Northwest

Grace and her family are going on a trip to see some interesting sites in a
city in the Pacific Northwest. The city is filled with exciting things to do and see.
There is a sentence on the travel website that describes it as a “must-see” spot!
Grace’s job was to plan their trip. She had a long list of what the family could do.
Grace said, “In the morning, we can go ice skating on the frozen lake. It faces
an iceberg. We could also walk to see the circle maze. There is a cedar totem
pole in the center.
“After lunch, we can race dog sleds! If we do that, we have to call and reserve
our spots. Only eight people can ride the sleds at one time,” Grace added.
“In the evening, we have to decide if we want to go to the dance or the palace
made of ice, ” she said. “We could also ice skate again,” Grace said with a smirk
on her face.
Her family was thrilled. She had picked something for everyone in the family.
That was a hard job.
Her mom said, “I think we will pass on skating twice. That would be a little
much. Everything else is just perfect. Thank you, Grace!”

Title: Hens and Pigs

Jed has pigs and hens on his land. Jed’s hens live in a big pen. The hens yak and strut in the pen. The pen has a shed in it. This is where the hens have beds. They can go in the shed to nap and to get out of the sun. Hens like to eat pests like grubs and bugs. Yum! The pig pen is just to the west of the hen shed. The pig pen has a pit of mud at one end. The pigs like to play, jump, and jog in the wet mud. They like to eat slop out of a vat, but they beg Jed for figs and yams. Jed’s hens and pigs are not pets. He can pat them, but they do nip. Jed’s pet is his cat. The cat is his pal and will go to the hen shed and the pig pen with Jed. Then she sits in the sun with Jed, and they rest.

Title: Take a Trip

If you do not want to be stuck at home this fall, plan a trip. Pick a date, select a spot, and go. You can stick close to home or travel the globe to a distant land. If you stick close, you could drive. If you go far, you could ride a bus, take a plane, or even fly in a blimp. You could visit a new state like Texas or a spot like the Grand Canyon. You could attend an event in your home state too. Hit the blacktop and plan for a nonstop trip. Safe travels! Make a note of things you want to do on your quest. It can be fun to branch out and try new things, not the same things you do at home. You may want to see a local ball game or a play about a brave robot. If you want to have a picnic, you could make a snack or a sandwich and take it with you. You could be brave and try a new plate for lunch. If you want some milk or punch on the go, take time to bring a thermos. You do not have to spend a lot. You and your pal could ride a bike to the lake and fly a kite in the blue sky or just bring a blanket and laze for a moment. You could go for a swim, catch a wave, or run in a zigzag on the white sand. If you go on a hike, bring your compass so you do not get lost. You may even find a cave, canyon, or tunnel to inspect. So, save your extra nickels in a can, and then fetch them and make it happen. I hope you rave about your trip when you come back.

Title: Three great mates

Sant made plans to meet his mate Spotty at the creek. He is happy, thinking
of all the fun games to play that sunny day.
Just then, Spotty popped out from a great big tree. Sant is happy to see his
mate, Spotty.
Spotty jumps in the creek. The creek is too deep for Sant the ant. Will Sant
reach Spotty? Sant can see some bark. It can carry Sant to Spotty.
Sant sings when he is happy. “My pal, Buzz-Bee, eats sweet treats.
Oh, so yummy in his tummy!” Spotty sways along to the song with glee.
“Did you say Buzz-Bee? That’s me!” It is Sant’s mate, Buzz.
“Great to see you Buzz! Please meet my mate, Spotty,” says Sant.
The team of three are messy from their fun at the creek. They need to brush
off the mud to get clean.
Buzz, Sant and Spotty eat sweet treats next to the creek.
Spotty, Buzz and Sant are three great mates. They agree to meet next week
by the great big tree.

Title: The Lost Raft

Brent’s raft is not in the shed. It is lost.
“Gram, can you tell me where my raft is?” said Brent.
Gram said, "No, bud. Go ask your mom and dad.”
“Mom! Dad! Can you help me? My raft is lost,” said Brent.
Mom said, “Is your raft still in the tub from when you were in the
bath? Did you stick it in the black bins out back? Is it in the grass by
the shed?”
Brent went to see. It was not there. Brent felt sad.
Dad said, “Did you check the loft? You went up there with the kids.”
He went to check the loft.
There it was! He was so glad!

Title: Jeans for Pru

Pru and her Aunt Sue live in an apartment in a suburb of the city. Pru and
her friends loved to ride the bus into the city to shop.
One day, Pru came running into the kitchen.
“Aunt Sue, may I have a little money, please?” asked Pru. “I’ll pay you
back as soon as I get my paycheck. My friends and I want to go shopping
at The Vintage Closet. We have a dance this weekend, and we want to
find something cute to wear.”
Aunt Sue was kind and gave Pru a few bucks. She said, “This should do
the trick! Happy hunting.”
The Vintage Closet is a thrift store on Main Street. Pru loved shopping at
thrift stores because the clothes were valued at a fair price. They also had
one-of-a-kind things!
Today, Pru was hoping to find some new jeans for the dance. Luckily, they
had a large supply of jeans in every hue. Pru wanted to find black skinny
jeans. She checked each rack. On the last rack, Pru saw these darling
jeans in just her size. They had a colorful cube patch on all of the pockets.
Cute! Cute! Cute!
Pru went to pay. She had just enough money to buy the jeans. She smiled
knowing that she got a bargain for her jeans and that they were perfect
to wear to the dance.

Title: This step that step

The sun comes up on the hill.
Nana, Pop and I huff and puff up the track.
That trunk went thud when it fell!
I must think, this step, then that step.
Nana and Pop help me get to the end of the trunk.
Moths flit this way and that. Some moths then land on a stump.
I sit still on the bank. It is a thrill to spot a frog!
We all thump, thump up the hill and get to the top.
I am hot! Nana has a damp cloth, that helps me.
All of us are glad to sit with some of Nana’s broth. Yum!

Title: The Carnival

The carnival is in town! Get your tickets, grab a friend, and head on down to the fair grounds. With so many options for excitement and entertainment, everyone is bound to have a great day at the carnival. If you are seeking adventure, head over to the midway. This is where you will find the rides. Slide down the bumpy super slide, walk through the spooky haunted house, or buckle up for a ride on the speedy roller coaster. If you get hungry, wander over to the food trucks. Here you will find every treat imaginable. A giant corndog, a funnel cake, and an ice-cold lemonade are the perfect carnival combination. If you get too hot and sweaty outside, step into the expo hall. Here you will meet farmers who can teach you about animals like chickens, pigs, and goats. You may even get to hold a baby chick! Also, there may be a cartoonist who will draw your caricature and a band playing music. At the end of the day, everyone gathers to watch the firework display in the night sky. This part is never a disappointment. Spending the day at the carnival is always enjoyable.

Title: Spreading Kindness

We all have good days and bad days. Good days are filled with brightness and happiness. On good days it is easy to be nice to our friends and everything seems fun. On good days annoying things don’t really bother us, and we feel a sense of calmness in our bodies. Bad days, on the other hand, are not so great. On bad days we may be filled with sadness or loneliness. Bad days can feel dark and scary. On bad days, it can be hard to be nice. On bad days lots of things might bother us, and we might not be in the mood for silliness. When we are having a good day, we have the energy we need to spread kindness to the people around us. We can lend a smile or a helping hand and share our brightness with others. In return, when we are having a bad day, we can lean on those kindness spreaders for the extra help we need. Because if everyone shares a little extra kindness on their good days, we can all help each other get through our bad days.

Title: Fay’s Birthday Party

Fay’s birthday is the fifth of May. She could hardly wait for this great day because that is
the day she was having the party she always wanted! Fay’s dad and grandma made a
list of things to do on a page in her writing tablet.
Fay’s Party
Invite friends.
Plan the games.
Play pin the Tail on the Mermaid.
•
Make bracelets and necklaces.
•
Face paint
•
Things to eat
cupcakes
•
They got to work. Fay made eight cards telling the date, time, and theme of the party.
She mailed them to her friends. Fay’s dad was an artist. To play Pin the Tail on the
Mermaid, he painted a mermaid and made the tails. Fay and her grandma took a break
from planning, to go on the subway to buy a mask for the game, the beads, the charms,
elastic string, and face paint in the city. Then they went to the bakery to buy cupcakes.
In the display case, there was a whole tray of yellow cupcakes with different colored
sparkles. Those were the ones she wanted! Before heading home, they stopped by the
butcher to buy Dad a steak for the grill. On the day of the party, it was raining, but
nothing could mess up this day. Fay put on her favorite shirt and shorts, while Dad fired
up the grill in the rain! Her grandma braided her hair into a fishtail. All of her friends
arrived and the fun began. After the party, Fay said it was the best day she had ever had!
